metadata.title: SPARC NGINX Reverse Proxy Component Definition

components.title: NGINX Reverse Proxy (ECS Sidecar)
components.description: NGINX reverse proxy running as a sidecar container in the ECS Fargate task definition. Listens on port 8080 (ALB-facing) and proxies to Rails/Puma on 127.0.0.1:3000. Built from nginx:1.27-alpine with custom configuration. Provides request buffering, gzip compression, header forwarding, static asset serving, and a lightweight health check endpoint. Configuration defined in AWS/ECS/nginx/. <!-- UPDATE: Insert NGINX image URL, container name, and ALB target group for your deployment. -->

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control implementations for NGINX reverse proxy

implemented-requirements.description: Boundary Protection: NGINX serves as the application-layer boundary between the ALB and Rails. It accepts connections only on port 8080 from the ALB and forwards to Rails on 127.0.0.1:3000 (not network-accessible). NGINX denies access to dotfiles and hidden paths (location ~ /\.). The client_max_body_size directive (100m) limits request body size, preventing oversized upload attacks. NGINX enforces proxy timeouts (connect: 60s, send: 60s, read: 60s). Reference: DISA SRG-NET-000364, SRG-APP-000141.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Configuration: nginx/conf.d/default.conf. Dotfile denial, body size limits, and timeout enforcement are in the server block.

implemented-requirements.description: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity: NGINX forwards security-relevant headers from the ALB to Rails: X-Forwarded-Proto (ensures Rails knows the original protocol is HTTPS), X-Forwarded-For (preserves client IP through the proxy chain), X-Real-IP (direct client address), and X-Forwarded-Port. Rails uses X-Forwarded-Proto to enforce FORCE_SSL=true. Internal traffic between NGINX and Rails is on localhost (127.0.0.1) within the same Fargate task — no network traversal. Reference: DISA SRG-NET-000062.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Header configuration in conf.d/default.conf proxy_set_header directives. TLS termination happens at the ALB; NGINX receives plaintext from the ALB.

implemented-requirements.description: Event Logging: NGINX access logs capture every HTTP request in a structured format: remote_addr, remote_user, time_local, request (method + URI + protocol), status, body_bytes_sent, http_referer, http_user_agent, x_forwarded_for, and request_time (rt=). Error logs capture NGINX-level errors at warn level. Both streams are sent to CloudWatch Logs via the awslogs driver with 'nginx' stream prefix, separate from Rails application logs ('rails' prefix). The /nginx-health endpoint has access_log off to reduce noise. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000089.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Log format defined in nginx/nginx.conf. Health check logging is suppressed to avoid polluting audit logs with ALB health check traffic.

implemented-requirements.description: Baseline Configuration: The NGINX configuration is baked into a Docker image built from nginx:1.27-alpine with only two configuration files (nginx.conf and conf.d/default.conf). The image is stored in a dedicated ECR repository ({project}-{env}-nginx) with immutable tags, ensuring reproducible deployments. Configuration changes require building and pushing a new image, creating a verifiable audit trail. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000133.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Dockerfile: AWS/ECS/nginx/Dockerfile. Configuration files: nginx/nginx.conf, nginx/conf.d/default.conf. ECR repo has scan-on-push and lifecycle policies.

implemented-requirements.description: Least Functionality: The NGINX container uses a minimal Alpine base image with only the NGINX binary and required libraries. Default configuration is removed and replaced with the SPARC-specific proxy configuration. The container runs as the non-root 'nginx' user with a read-only root filesystem (readonlyRootFilesystem=true), preventing any runtime filesystem modification. PID file is written to /tmp (writable without root). Only port 8080 is exposed. No additional modules, plugins, or services are installed. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000141.
implemented-requirements.remarks: readonlyRootFilesystem=true in task definition. Dockerfile runs as nginx user. Only two config files are copied. No build tools or unnecessary binaries.

implemented-requirements.description: Information Input Validation: NGINX provides a dedicated health check endpoint (/nginx-health) that returns HTTP 200 with a plain text response without proxying to Rails. This allows the ALB to verify NGINX availability independently. The ALB target group health check is configured to hit /nginx-health, ensuring the reverse proxy layer is functional before routing traffic. Unhealthy tasks (where NGINX is down) are automatically deregistered. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000251.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Health check in conf.d/default.conf: location /nginx-health returns 200. ALB health_check_path defaults to /nginx-health.

implemented-requirements.description: Denial-of-Service Protection: NGINX provides request buffering (proxy_buffering on, proxy_buffer_size 8k, proxy_buffers 16 8k) to protect Rails from slow clients. The client_max_body_size 100m limit prevents oversized request attacks. Proxy timeouts (60s connect/send/read) prevent connection exhaustion. Gzip compression reduces bandwidth consumption. Combined with ALB connection limits and AWS Shield Standard, this provides layered DoS protection. Reference: DISA SRG-NET-000362.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Buffering, body size limits, and timeouts in conf.d/default.conf. Gzip configuration in nginx.conf.
